convertibility_reason: Uses two custom indicators (VininI_Trend_LRMA and ChangeOfVolatility via iCustom) and depends on two external .mqh libraries (SmoothAlgorithms.mqh, TradeAlgorithms.mqh) for smoothing algorithms and trade execution logic. Custom indicators require recreation in Python.

position_sizing.conditional_logic: negative MM value = fixed lot size (abs value), positive MM value = deposit fraction for position sizing; handled by TradeAlgorithms.mqh

custom_logic_notes: Two algorithm modes selectable via Mode input: BREAKDOWN (indicator crosses UpLevel/DnLevel levels) and TWIST (indicator changes direction). ChangeOfVolatility custom indicator acts as a trend-strength filter requiring Trend[0] > MaxTrendLevel before any entry. The version with underscore suffix (exp_vinini_trend_lrma_.mq5) lacks the ChangeOfVolatility filter entirely - it uses only VininI_Trend_LRMA with simpler entry conditions. SignalBar parameter controls which bar index is used for signal detection (0=current, 1=previous completed bar). Recount mechanism retries signal detection if CopyBuffer fails. Position management (open/close) is delegated to TradeAlgorithms.mqh library functions.
python_conversion_notes: Two custom indicators must be reimplemented: VininI_Trend_LRMA (uses CXMA class from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh with 9 smoothing methods including JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) and ChangeOfVolatility (momentum-based volatility filter). The SmoothAlgorithms.mqh library contains proprietary smoothing algorithms (JJMA, JurX, ParMA, T3, VIDYA, AMA) that have no standard Python equivalents - these must be ported from MQL5 source. TradeAlgorithms.mqh handles position sizing (conditional fixed-lot vs deposit-fraction), order placement with deviation, and position closing - this must be replaced with broker API calls. The two EA variants differ significantly: the underscore version omits ChangeOfVolatility entirely and has simpler entry rules without the MaxTrendLevel filter. SL/TP are in points (not pips) so digit adjustment depends on broker; no explicit 5-digit adjustment logic is present in the EA code itself.
